name: flu-lung-crossparadigm
claim: REVISED 2026-11-05 (reviewer feedback: vertex CD8/NK floated free of the tissue): vertex immune cells are now SMALLER POLYGONS IN THE EPITHELIAL SHEET, attached at the tissue margin and moving along it by neighbour exchange, as the CPM immune pool wets the epithelial edge; reconnect resolves merged rosettes faster (p_4 = 1, T1 at 0.2 x side); motilities re-calibrated under the no-fold cap. On this substrate FATE still falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross 0.948 vs 0.926-0.960), but infected-patch OCCUPANCY (IoU 0.053, below both baselines 0.100 / 0.299) and LOCATION (centroid distance 5.7 vs 3.3 um) now separate the backends -- a candidate substrate signal, not yet causally attributed. Earlier reading (2026-10-28, overlay immune layer) kept for provenance: The ONE backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint compiles to BOTH the CPM (viva-cpm) and vertex (vivarium-tyssue) substrates and runs the Sego model WITH NAMED DEVIATIONS (V/L/C/F producers absent, latent-pool recruitment approximation) end-to-end on each. RE-RUN 2026-10-28 on the REVISED vertex substrate: a hexagonal one-polygon-per-cell sheet, immune overlay, auto_reconnect, per-pair tension, domain walls, and CPM-calibrated motility under a no-fold constraint. Vertex cells now move within the tissue and exchange neighbours, though the epithelium wanders ~5x less than on the CPM. Replicate runs are now also stochastic in their MECHANICS, so the same-backend null control includes mechanical noise. Against that null, cell FATE, infected-patch OCCUPANCY and patch LOCATION all fall inside the same-backend seed spread (fail to reject). The one candidate substrate signal left: the vertex I-count leaves the narrow CPM 3-seed envelope for ~45% of steps by N=400.
experiment: Compile `workspace/blueprints/influenza_sego2022.yaml` onto CPM and vertex and run the full model at a tractable reduced scale (a 50x50-site patch, a 6x6 epithelial block + a 12-cell pre-placed latent immune pool). For >=3 CPM rules-seeds AND the vertex backend, compute: (1) per-cell fate agreement over the t0 cohort, reported RELATIVE to the same-backend (CPM-vs-CPM) seed baseline; (2) dynamics -- the vertex I-count trajectory checked for the fraction of steps inside the CPM >=3-seed stochastic envelope (a non-circular check); (3) spatial pattern -- infected-patch area/centroid/Rg + occupancy IoU, with the representation confound controlled by confirming the final-frame cell areas match across backends. A THIRD paradigm, a center-based model (viva-munk), is compiled from the same blueprint and shown as a third panel in spatial_playback (and as a third series in dynamics_overlay, with pairwise divergence maps); its quantitative three-way pairwise statistics are carried by the crossparadigm-equivalence study. Render spatial_playback, dynamics_overlay and divergence. Headline figures are regenerated by `scripts/regen_capstone_metrics.py` (N=400, now with a center-based row); the behavior test pins the baseline-relative relationship at N=150.
result:
RE-RUN 2026-11-05 (in-sheet immune polygons, re-calibrated motility; N=400, 3 CPM x 3 vertex seeds, scripts/regen_capstone_metrics.py): - Fate agreement: cross 0.948 (0.904-0.996) between the same-backend baselines
  (CPM-vs-CPM 0.926 [0.901-0.955]; vertex-vs-vertex 0.960 [0.950-0.976]) -> fail to reject.
- Infected-patch occupancy IoU: cross 0.053 (0.005-0.150), BELOW both baselines (CPM
  0.100, vertex 0.299) -> candidate signal.
- Patch centroid distance: 5.7 um cross (2.0-8.6) vs 3.3 um same-backend CPM (2.6-4.8). - Final mean EPITHELIAL cell area: CPM 23.42, vertex 21.98 (ratio 0.94; the immune
  polygons are half-size by design, so the representation check is epithelium-only).
- Vertex (seed 0) I-count inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 55% of steps. - 74 vertex neighbour exchanges over the run (shown in the playback). The CI behavior test (N=150) still passes. Earlier result (2026-10-28, overlay immune layer), superseded: Both backends run the Sego model (with named deviations) end-to-end. N=400, 3 CPM x 3 vertex seeds: - Fate agreement: cross 0.938 (0.899-0.993) lies between the same-backend baselines
  (CPM-vs-CPM 0.926 [0.901-0.955]; vertex-vs-vertex 0.944 [0.921-0.973]).
- Infected-patch occupancy IoU: cross 0.135 (0.038-0.277), between CPM 0.100 and
  vertex 0.175.
- Patch centroid distance: 3.6 um cross vs 3.3 um same-backend CPM. - Final mean cell area: CPM 24.67, vertex 23.13 (ratio 0.94). - The vertex (seed 0) I-count is inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 55% of steps (100%
  at N=150).
At the CI scale (N=150): cross fate 0.987 vs same-backend CPM 0.976, area ratio 0.96. Superseded readings: the old "IoU below both baselines" signal came from mechanically deterministic replicates, and the intermediate "location" signal from an over-mobile (folding) vertex sheet; neither survives. CONCLUSION: on fate, occupancy and location we fail to reject a substrate difference (a null, not equality). Late I-count dynamics are the remaining candidate, to test with more CPM seeds (a wider envelope) and larger scale.

purpose.question: Does one backend-neutral blueprint reproduce the Sego 2022 influenza model on two different mechanical substrates, and -- judged against same-backend seed noise -- do the substrates diverge?
purpose.mechanism: The epithelial rates, four reaction-diffusion fields, Price-2015 systemic ODE (fed live by CellCountStep) and latent-pool immune recruitment are compiled identically onto both backends; only the single mechanics node differs (CPM Metropolis flips vs tyssue vertex relaxation). If the substrate mattered beyond noise, the cross-backend metrics would fall OUTSIDE the same-backend seed spread.
purpose.expected_outcome: Cross-backend fate and patch-location metrics within the same-backend seed envelope (backend-neutral), with any residual difference small and attributable to stochastic scatter rather than the substrate.

key_assumptions: The comparison is baseline-relative: cross-backend is judged against the same-backend seed spread, never against zero.

Seed provenance: the headline N=400 table (scripts/regen_capstone_metrics.py) builds the same-backend baselines from 3 CPM seeds {0,1,2} AND 3 vertex seeds {0,1,2}, and the cross term from all 9 CPM*vertex pairs (3x3). The lighter CI behavior test (N=150) pins the same relationship with CPM seeds {0,1,2} vs vertex seed 0.

Vertex is near-degenerate across rules-seeds at this scale: the slow epidemic yields ~identical vertex I-counts for different seeds (vertex-vs-vertex agreement 0.935-0.949, sd 0.006, vs CPM sd 0.025), so the vertex seed count barely affects the result -- which is why the CI test can use a single vertex seed without changing the conclusion.

Reduced scale: a 50x50-site patch with a 6x6 epithelial block (NOT paper scale); headline N=400 (= 400 MCS = ~6.7 h of SIMULATED time at 60 s/MCS; ~45 s wall-clock for the full 6-run regen script), CI test N=150.
Immune recruitment is activation of a PRE-PLACED LATENT pool at the tissue margin (ruling T20-RECRUIT), not from-nothing insertion.
The systemic-ODE inputs V/L/C/F have NO producer yet and sit at 0 (Task 21 follow-up), so the ODE recruitment drive is weak and the latent pool is barely activated at this scale.
Sego rates are carried verbatim (no tuning); at faithful rates the infection probability is ~0.004/step, so the epidemic is a slow onset.
1 grid unit = 1 um (grid_resolution_um = 1); the vertex Voronoi t0 faces are larger (~46) but relax to the target (~25) by the end, so the final-frame spatial comparison is fair.

limitations: REVIEW: biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is NOT validated here -- a CPM self-envelope is an internal consistency check, not a match to digitized Sego figures/measured flu-lung data (Stage 4 / BP-08).
REVIEW: 'runs the model' carries NAMED DEVIATIONS -- V/L/C/F have no producer (sit at 0) and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation; quantify their effect by ablation (Stage 4 / BP-05).
Reduced scale + modest steps: a demonstration, not paper scale; the epidemic is in slow onset, so any substrate signal is small relative to seed noise.
The headline is a NULL result on fate and occupancy (fail to reject), which is scale-dependent: absence of evidence here is not proof the substrates never diverge.
Immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation (T20-RECRUIT); at this scale the ODE drive rounds to ~0 activations, so the immune arm (and the calibrated vertex chemotaxis) is barely exercised.
The systemic-ODE inputs V/L/C/F have no producer (Task 21) and sit at 0, further weakening the recruitment drive.
Parameters are the faithful Sego 2022 values (no tuning of the biology); the vertex MECHANICS knobs are calibrated to CPM behaviour (adhesion-calibration), never to make the fates agree.
The dynamics acceptance band is the CPM 3-seed stochastic envelope (narrow with 3 seeds), NOT a digitized Sego 2022 figure.
Immune contact differs by design: same-layer edge contact on CPM vs overlay overlap area on vertex.
The vertex epithelium wanders ~5x less than the CPM's (motility capped so the mesh never folds; see adhesion-calibration).

report.title: Flu-lung cross-paradigm: one blueprint, three substrates; fate within seed noise, center-based added
report.verdict:
THREE-WAY (center-based added 2026-11-06). The same canonical blueprint now compiles to a THIRD mechanical substrate — a center-based model (viva-munk: circular rigid bodies, area-matched, hard-disc relaxation) via local:MunkBackend — shown as a third panel in the spatial playback and scored pairwise alongside CPM and vertex. The quantitative null-control table below remains the CPM↔vertex capstone measurement; the full three-way pairwise statistics (fate EQUIVALENT across all three pairs; spatial not, with the center-based model the most divergent) live in the crossparadigm-equivalence study. Original CPM↔vertex verdict follows.
RE-RUN on the revised vertex substrate (2026-10-28 review: hexagonal one-polygon- per-cell sheet, immune overlay, auto_reconnect, per-pair tension, domain walls, CPM-calibrated motility capped so the mesh never folds). Vertex cells now move within the tissue and exchange neighbours. Replicates are mechanics-stochastic on both backends. The single Sego 2022 blueprint runs the Sego model WITH NAMED DEVIATIONS on both substrates. Judged against the same-backend seed null control (N=400), cross-backend fate agreement (0.938 between 0.926 / 0.944), occupancy IoU (0.135 between 0.100 / 0.175) and infected-patch location (3.6 vs 3.3 um) all lie within seed noise. We therefore FAIL TO REJECT a substrate difference on all three. The earlier candidate signals (IoU, then location) did not survive. The remaining candidate is late dynamics: the vertex I-count is inside the narrow 3-seed CPM envelope at 55% of steps by N=400 (100% at N=150). Caveats: reduced scale, 3 x 3 seeds, and the vertex epithelium wanders ~5x less than the CPM's (mesh-validity cap).
report.main_insight: Sharing the mechanism byte-for-byte isolates the mechanical substrate as the only possible source of difference. Once both substrates move their cells and replicates differ mechanically, fate, occupancy and location differences are inside seed noise. Each earlier "candidate signal" was an artifact of a deterministic null or of the vertex mechanics, which is why the null control has to carry mechanical noise.
report.caveat: A null (fail-to-reject) result at reduced scale with 3 x 3 seeds; the CPM envelope is narrow; the vertex epithelium is less fluid than the CPM's; the immune arm is barely exercised (latent pool + producer-less ODE inputs); the band is the CPM stochastic envelope, not a Sego figure.

findings.statement: On the revised vertex substrate with mechanics-stochastic replicates, cross-backend fate agreement (0.938), infected-patch occupancy IoU (0.135) and patch location (3.6 um) all lie within the same-backend baselines (0.926/0.944; 0.100/0.175; 3.3 um), so we fail to reject a substrate difference on any of them.

evidence.observed: N=400: fate cross 0.938 vs same CPM 0.926 / vertex 0.944; IoU cross 0.135 vs 0.100 / 0.175; centroid 3.60 vs 3.33 um; area ratio 0.94; N=150 cross 0.987 vs same 0.976

findings.explanation: Fate is computed by the shared mechanism; the substrate enters only via field sampling + contact surface.
findings.next_action: more seeds + larger scale; Stage 4 producers (V/L/C/F)

findings.statement: The vertex I-count stays inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 100% of steps to N=150 but only 55% by N=400 -- a candidate late-dynamics substrate signal, not yet separated from the narrowness of a 3-seed envelope.

evidence.observed: vertex in-band 0.551 at N=400, 1.0 at N=150

findings.explanation: Infection spread later in the run may depend on each substrate's cell motility and contact geometry.
findings.next_action: widen the envelope with more CPM seeds; compare against a vertex-seed envelope

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED (2026-10-28, revised vertex substrate). On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross fate 0.942 vs CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um; vertex 100% inside the CPM envelope), so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate difference -- a null result, not proof of equality.

evidence.observed: cross 0.942 (0.890-1.000) vs same-backend CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; vertex in-band 1.0; N=150 cross == same == 0.987

expected.range: cross within the same-backend seed spread (null control)

findings.explanation: Fate is computed by the shared field/rules/ODE; the substrate enters only via centroid field-sampling + contact-surface, whose effect is not separable from seed noise at this scale/seed count.
findings.next_action: drive the ODE V/L/C/F producers (Task 21) and re-test at larger scale / more vertex seeds, where a substrate effect could become detectable

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED (2026-10-28): did not survive mechanics-stochastic replicates. Raw infected-patch occupancy IoU is the ONE metric trending below BOTH same-backend baselines (cross 0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212, ~25-35% lower). It is NOT a representation artifact (final mean areas match: CPM 24.67 vs vertex 24.51), so it is flagged as a CANDIDATE weak substrate signal -- not attributed to seed noise, which is untested -- to be checked at larger scale / more seeds.

evidence.observed: final area ratio 0.99; IoU_I cross 0.165 vs same-backend CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um

findings.explanation: Both baselines are low (single-patch scatter), but the cross term sits below both; the (old) vertex Voronoi faces relaxed to target, ruling out the t0 size confound.
findings.next_action: test the IoU gap with more vertex seeds + a larger/longer run before calling it signal or noise; report IoU only with its same-backend baseline

findings.statement: At faithful Sego rates the per-step infection probability is ~0.004 and the ODE recruitment inflow rounds to ~0 activations, so at reduced scale the epidemic is a slow onset and the latent immune pool is barely activated.

evidence.observed: virus-field integral grows 0 -> ~180 over 400 steps; H/I/D ~30/5/1 (CPM); activations = 0

findings.explanation: Faithful rates + reduced scale + producer-less ODE inputs -> weak drive; not tuned up (anti-goal).
findings.next_action: add the V/L/C/F producers and/or run longer; keep rates faithful
